**Head of Engineering Job Description:** Scope, Impact & Qualifications Reports to: CEO Level: Executive (CTO-equivalent scope) Org size: ~25 engineers Time split: 70% Product / 30% Discipline ROLE SUMMARY The Head of Engineering owns the technical outcomes of Maestro's entire product suite while also serving as the top of the engineering discipline ladder: every engineering manager and individual contributor ultimately ladders up to this role. The position deliberately splits attention: 70% product execution, 30% discipline accountability. Product delivery is the immediate, ongoing accountability; discipline work compounds over time and requires protected but smaller blocks of focus so it doesn't get crowded out by delivery pressure. This role sits at the center of Maestro's matrix structure, accountable for craft quality and standards company-wide, while ensuring embedded engineering talent on each product team is pointed at the right priorities.
  
  
**SCOPE • Org reach:** all engineering leads across all product lines report into this role (directly or via a lead layer), the senior-most engineering accountability in the company. • Product surface: full product suite, every active product line's engineering output. • Discipline surface: engineering-wide standards, tooling, and process, independent of which product team an engineer sits on. THE 70%: PRODUCT ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering is the single accountable owner for engineering execution across Maestro's product portfolio.
  
  
**What this looks like day to day:** • Partners with the engineering leads of every product line to ensure their teams are resourced against the right priorities: not just busy, but correctly sequenced. • Accountable for ensuring product strategy and roadmap direction are translated into clear, actionable engineering plans, serving as the connective layer between Product and Delivery leadership and the engineering organization, primarily through engineering leads embedded within product teams. • Accountable for applying technical judgment to turn high-level strategic priorities into concrete technical execution plans, enabling and guiding engineering leads to scope, sequence, and de-risk delivery across their product areas. • Identifies where product priorities and engineering capacity are misaligned across teams and resolves the tradeoff, including cross-team resourcing calls.
  
  

* Is the escalation point when a product line's engineering execution is off track, and is accountable for getting it back on track. Impact: Every product line ships against strategy, not just against what's easiest to build. Product and Delivery leaders have one accountable engineering partner instead of negotiating separately with each product line's lead. THE 30%: DISCIPLINE ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering owns what "good engineering" means at Maestro, independent of the product line.

**What this looks like day to day:** • Sets and maintains company-wide engineering standards (code quality, architecture principles, technical debt posture). • Owns cross-cutting technical initiatives that no single product team should solve independently, e.g. product suite services and universal QA automation. • Defines how AI tooling is used across engineering, including guardrails to ensure AI usage improves output quality and velocity rather than introducing risk or degrading craft.
  
  

* Identifies and removes friction in how engineering work gets done company-wide, streamlining processes that slow every team down in the same way. • Is the ultimate accountable owner for engineering management practice (how EMs lead, how performance is evaluated, how the craft is grown) even where day-to-day people management is embedded in product teams. Impact: Engineering quality, velocity, and management practice don't fragment by product line. An engineer's experience of "how we build software here" is consistent no matter which team they're on, and the org gets the benefits of scale (shared tooling, shared standards) instead of each team reinventing its own.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Engineers across the organization deliver flawless technical execution that earns long-term client retention and supports growth. • Product lines are resourced against strategic priority, with tradeoffs made explicitly rather than by default. • Engineering leads across product lines operate with a shared technical bar and shared tooling. • Company-wide initiatives (QA automation, AI usage standards) ship and get adopted, not just get designed.
  
  

* Engineering management practice is consistent and healthy across the org, even though EMs are embedded in product teams day to day. QUALIFICATIONS Maestro hires for demonstrated capability, not years-of-service checkboxes. The bar below is competency-based: what someone needs to be able to do, not how long they've been doing it. Required competencies: • Has personally carried end-to-end accountability for engineering delivery across more than one product or team simultaneously: not just led a single team, but balanced competing priorities across several.
* Can translate ambiguous, high-level strategy (from product, business, or leadership) into a technical execution plan that engineers can actually build against, without needing someone else to do that translation. • Has designed or materially improved an engineering standard, process, or tooling investment that worked across teams (not a single-team fix) and can point to the before/after. • Comfortably operates in a matrixed environment, influencing and aligning engineering leads, their teams, and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on formal authority. • Has hands-on technical depth sufficient to earn credibility with senior engineers and to personally evaluate technical tradeoffs.

This is not a purely managerial role. • Has direct experience managing or mentoring engineering managers, not only individual contributors. • Demonstrates sound judgment on when to standardize company-wide versus when to let product teams operate with autonomy. Strongly preferred: • Experience operating at this scope inside a company of comparable size (roughly 15 to 50 engineers), where formal process is lighter and judgment calls happen more often than policy lookups.
  
  

* Direct experience setting a company's approach to AI-assisted engineering (tooling choices, guardrails, or usage standards) rather than just using AI tools personally. • A track record of building or scaling QA automation, testing strategy, or release process across multiple teams. • Experience partnering directly with Product and Delivery leadership as a peer, not just receiving requirements from them. • Experience leading engineering for always-on, customer-facing digital products or live-service platforms, where availability, release discipline, observability, incident response, and rapid cross-functional coordination directly affect the end-user experience and client retention.

**What we're explicitly not requiring:** • A specific prior title (VP Engineering, CTO, etc.). We care about scope actually carried, not the title it came with. • A minimum years-of-experience threshold. Competency and evidence of impact matter more than tenure.
  
  

* Deep expertise in every technology in Maestro's stack. Technical judgment and the ability to evaluate tradeoffs matter more than hands-on fluency in any one language or framework.

Business Architecture is a foundational discipline of the practice. The Senior Director, Software & Services Strategy will report directly to the VP, Strategy, Power and serve as the enterprise strategist and business architect for the convergence of software, controls, industrial data, artificial intelligence, and lifecycle services across the Power Segment.

The role will help Power evolve from a model centered primarily on equipment control, software products, and event-based service delivery toward an integrated growth system that uses proprietary industrial context, trusted intelligence, validated action, and service execution to improve customer availability, reliability, productivity, operating economics, and lifecycle value.

This leader will not replace the operating accountability of Services or Software & Controls Solutions. **Why the Role Is Needed**
==========================

Power’s Services business represents a foundational long-term profit pool. Software & Controls Solutions is smaller today from a P&L perspective but has significant growth ambitions and provides capabilities that can reshape the future economics and differentiation of Services. The critical strategic question is therefore broader than how to grow software as a standalone business.

* Industrial software firms, systems integrators, hyperscalers, OEMs, and AI-native entrants are increasingly competing to own the customer’s data context, workflow layer, decision interface, and transformation agenda.

* GE Vernova’s differentiated starting point is its installed base, controls authority, equipment and fleet knowledge, service history, customer relationships, and ability to translate insight into safe, validated action.

* Without coordinated leadership, fragmented investment, unclear commercial credit, competing roadmaps, and slow cross-business decisions could prevent Power from converting those assets into durable growth.

* The role creates a single point of accountability for translating the strategy into a portfolio of customer-backed ventures and scalable operating-model choices.

  
  

**Mission**

**Build the strategy, operating model, partnerships, commercial architecture, and transformation portfolio required for Software, Controls, AI, Industrial Data, and Services to operate as one integrated growth system.**

**Job Description**

The Project Manager Operations Consultant/ Circuit Analyst position is responsible for providing technical and administrative support within the Radio Team and in cooperation with the EIS circuit team of a sensitive Federal customer. The role further includes coordinating operations to include order/initiate provisioning, execute decommissioning, and tracking status of the appropriate voice circuits, data circuits, and POTS lines on time and in accordance with customer procedures. * Prepare and present weekly executive status dashboards for OCI leadership regarding the RAD initiative, offering detailed breakdowns of outstanding deliverables, TTUs, and site construction timelines.
* Lead coordination for National Special Security Event (NSSE) circuit requests alongside Field Technicians, serving as OCI's principal point of contact for EIS and AT&T during high-priority operations.
* Maintain and continuously audit the global circuit inventory database, collaborating with the CIO, onsite network engineering teams, and EIS to reconcile data gaps and ensure full record integrity.
* Administer and manage telecom circuits for the communications program by processing, auditing, analyzing, organizing, and correcting telecommunications billing; validating discounts; ensuring accurate department billing; monitoring the disconnection of unused lines and circuits; and reporting to the on-site Senior Manager of the Field Service Team.

The Network Operations Center (NOC) Manager is responsible for establishing and managing a high-performing, 24/7 operational support organization responsible for monitoring infrastructure, managing customer support requests, coordinating incident response, and ensuring exceptional service delivery.

This is a hands-on leadership position requiring a combination of technical expertise, operational discipline, customer service leadership, and organizational development.

The NOC Manager will initially focus on building the Austin NOC operation, including recruiting personnel, establishing staffing schedules, implementing operating procedures, defining escalation processes, and developing the tools and reporting necessary to manage a growing global infrastructure environment.

Once operational, the NOC Manager will have direct accountability for the performance of the NOC, including ticket response times, ticket resolution coordination, incident escalation, customer communications, shift coverage, and operational reporting.

A primary responsibility of this position is ensuring that every customer support ticket receives timely attention, accurate classification, appropriate escalation, consistent follow-through, and documented resolution.

The NOC Manager must establish a culture in which tickets are actively managed from creation through closure, regardless of which technical department is responsible for performing the underlying work.

The successful candidate will understand that the NOC is not simply a monitoring organization. It is the central coordination point for customer-impacting operational issues across Cirrascale's infrastructure.

The NOC Manager will work closely with Engineering, Data Center Operations, Infrastructure Deployment, Network Engineering, Systems Engineering, Hardware Support, and RMA personnel to ensure issues are resolved efficiently and customers remain informed.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**NOC Development, Organization, Leadership, and Change Management**

* Lead the establishment and operational development of Cirrascale's Network Operations Center in Austin, Texas.
* Develop the organizational structure required to support continuous 24/7/365 infrastructure monitoring and customer support.
* Participate in recruiting, interviewing, selecting, onboarding, and training NOC personnel.
* Establish staffing requirements, shift schedules, and coverage plans based on ticket volumes, infrastructure growth, and customer service commitments.
* Develop structured onboarding and training programs to ensure employees can perform their responsibilities consistently and independently.
* Establish shift turnover procedures to ensure continuity of operations and communication of unresolved incidents, open tickets, customer commitments, and operational risks.
* Build a culture of accountability, professionalism, technical competency, teamwork, and exceptional customer service.
* Conduct performance reviews, coaching sessions, and employee development activities.
* Establish and oversee operational change management processes for production infrastructure.
* Ensure the NOC has visibility into scheduled maintenance, approved infrastructure changes, and anticipated service impacts.
* Ensure monitoring, documentation, escalation contacts, and support procedures are established before new systems, infrastructure expansions, and customer deployments are transitioned into production.
* Establish procedures for identifying, monitoring, and escalating incidents associated with recent infrastructure changes.

**Ticket Management and Service Desk Operations**

Ticket management is the primary responsibility of the NOC Manager. The individual must maintain complete operational visibility into customer and internal support activities.

* Oversee the complete lifecycle of all customers and internally generated operational support tickets.
* Continuously monitor ticket queues for unassigned, aging, stalled, improperly prioritized, or unresolved tickets.
* Establish response-time, escalation, and resolution expectations consistent with customer service-level agreements.
* Ensure tickets are properly documented and not closed prematurely or without adequate resolution.
* Establish escalation procedures for tickets exceeding response or resolution targets.
* Establish standardized ticket documentation requirements, including troubleshooting steps, technical findings, escalation history, customer communications, and final resolution.
* Identify recurring ticket categories and coordinate corrective actions to reduce repeat issues.
* Establish procedures for reopening tickets when reported issues have not been fully resolved.

The NOC Manager must understand ticket volumes, backlog conditions, outstanding customer issues, assigned ownership, and the actions being taken to resolve them at any given time.

**Incident Management, Operational Escalation, Planned Maintenance**

* Establish and manage incident detection, classification, response, escalation, and resolution procedures.
* Develop clearly defined incident severity levels and escalation requirements.
* Ensure critical incidents receive immediate attention and are escalated according to established procedures.
* Coordinate incident response across Engineering, Infrastructure Operations, Data Center Operations, and external service providers.
* Serve as an operational escalation point during significant service interruptions.
* Maintain clear accountability for incident ownership, response coordination, and resolution.
* Ensure incident activities are documented accurately, including timelines, actions taken, communications, and resolution details.
* Coordinate post-incident reviews and root cause analysis with the appropriate technical teams.
* Track corrective actions resulting from incidents and ensure identified problems are addressed.
* Ensure unresolved incidents are appropriately communicated during shift transitions and customer-impacting incidents receive proper follow-up.
* Manage and monitor the planned maintenance schedule across all sites and ensure customers are notified and go smoothly.
* Coordinate customer notifications and internal communications associated with planned maintenance and infrastructure changes.

**Cross-Functional Operational Coordination**

The NOC serves as a central coordination function within Cirrascale's Operations organization. The NOC manager owns this piece.

* Coordinate with Network Engineering on connectivity issues, network outages, routing problems, and equipment failures.
* Work with Systems Engineering on server failures, operating system issues, and hardware-related incidents.
* Coordinate with Data Center Operations and remote technicians for physical troubleshooting and hardware replacement activities.
* Work with RMA and hardware support personnel to track failed components, replacement parts, and repair activities.

**About Neurophos**
===================

The demand for new data centers and AI compute is rapidly outpacing the planet's energy capacity. Digital solutions are hitting a power wall as we approach the physical limits of traditional silicon. Conquering this bottleneck means rethinking the fundamental architecture of inference compute. The industry's current path can't meet the need, so we're taking a different approach.

Instead of traditional electronic circuits, we use silicon photonics and an active, programmable metasurface to perform matrix multiplications at the speed of light. Our optical cells are 10,000x smaller than traditional photonic components, enabling unprecedented density. By using photonics instead of electricity, our chips become more efficient as they scale. This architecture will deliver up to 100 times the energy efficiency of existing solutions while significantly improving performance for large-scale AI inference.

We’ve assembled a world-class team of industry veterans and recently raised a $110M Series A led by Gates Frontier. Participants include M12 (Microsoft’s Venture Fund), Carbon Direct Capital, Aramco Ventures, Bosch Ventures, Tectonic Ventures, Space Capital, and others.

A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.

* Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries—so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
* Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
* Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
* Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives—expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations—that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
* Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations—combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
* Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
* Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
* Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
* Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
* Over your first 6–12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts—carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.

What We Look For
  
  

* Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture—ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS—with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.
* Operational Ownership: proven ability to run alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and technical inquiries across a set of accounts, balancing reactive operational work with proactive initiatives.
* Ownership & Autonomy: proven ability to independently scope and deliver complex, open-ended technical work, and to partner with stakeholders on launch initiatives, with strong project management and follow-through.
* API Expertise: deep understanding of RESTful APIs, webhooks, and the HTTP protocol, with hands-on experience using tools like Postman to debug and validate integrations.
* Architecture Fluency: Experience in API integrations and the ability to design custom solutions on top of them to solve complex merchant challenges.
* Coding & Code Fluency: ability to read and understand production-level code (HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and ideally one server-side language such as Python) and to author new, novel queries to diagnose merchant or system issues.
* Troubleshooting Acumen: ability to diagnose issues using browser developer consoles, log analysis and observability platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Chronosphere), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, Notion).
* Technical Communication: excellent verbal and written communication; able to tailor explanations to both non-technical leaders and technical teams, read a room and adjust in real time, and synthesize technical challenges back to internal teams.
* Relationship Management: ability to discover and develop relationships with technical decision-makers, secure written consensus on integration milestones, and drive cross-team collaboration.
* Leadership & Mentorship: demonstrated ability to mentor teammates, set best practices, and lead technical initiatives; a growth mindset with self-awareness and a habit of seeking and acting on feedback.

Nice to Have
  
  

* Familiarity with the payments ecosystem.
* Familiarity with web/mobile application architecture.
* Experience implementing or customizing e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, or in-store point-of-sale systems.
* Experience acting as a technical lead on cross-functional projects and influencing product roadmaps.

**Description**
At 1898 & Co., we are helping shape the future of transmission systems across North America. Our Transmission Planning & Power Systems Analysis (TPPSA) team works with investor-owned utilities, public power entities, developers, and ISOs/RTOs to address increasingly complex grid planning and infrastructure challenges.
  
  
We are seeking a Project Delivery Director to provide leadership and oversight for project delivery within our TPPSA business line. This position will help establish and maintain consistent project-delivery practices, strengthen the performance and development of our Project Delivery Managers, and support the successful execution of a growing portfolio of consulting engagements.
  
  
The Project Delivery Director will work closely with business-line leadership, Project Delivery Managers, technical leaders, project managers, and other 1898 & Co. leaders to improve project outcomes, manage delivery risk, and support profitable growth. The successful candidate will combine strong project-delivery experience with practical leadership, sound business judgment, and the ability to work across teams.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**
Project Delivery Leadership
  
  

* Provide leadership and oversight for project delivery across the TPPSA portfolio.
* Establish clear expectations and consistent practices for project planning, execution, monitoring, forecasting, and closeout.
* Support project delivery teams and project managers in developing practical execution strategies for complex consulting engagements.
* Review project performance and help teams identify and address issues related to scope, schedule, budget, staffing, quality, and client commitments.
* Promote accountability for project results while helping teams resolve delivery challenges early.
* Support the consistent use of applicable project-delivery tools, systems, processes, and performance measures.
* Help define and advance project-delivery priorities that are aligned with business-line and company objectives.

Project Performance and Risk Management
  
  

* Monitor the health and performance of the project portfolio, including financial results, schedule performance, resource needs, quality, and delivery risk.
* Work with project teams to develop recovery plans for projects that are not meeting expectations.
* Support effective project initiation, including alignment on scope, responsibilities, staffing, schedule, budget, and client expectations.
* Help teams manage scope changes, contract requirements, project risks, and commercial considerations throughout project execution.
* Identify recurring delivery challenges and lead improvements that strengthen project performance across the business line.
* Support appropriate quality-management and review processes for project deliverables.
* Elevate significant project risks and performance concerns to business-line leadership when appropriate.

Project Delivery Manager Development
  
  

* Provide leadership, coaching, and support to project delivery teams within TPPSA.
* Support the selection, onboarding, and development of employees serving in project-delivery leadership positions.
* Facilitate the sharing of lessons learned, delivery practices, and practical tools across projects and teams.
* Help project delivery teams strengthen their capabilities in financial management, forecasting, risk management, client communication, team leadership, and project controls.
* Provide direct, constructive feedback that supports individual development and improves project outcomes.

Resource and Operational Coordination
  
  

* Work with business-line leaders and project teams to understand workload, staffing requirements, and delivery priorities.
* Help identify and resolve resource constraints that could affect project commitments or portfolio performance.
* Support alignment among project scope, staffing plans, schedules, and budgets.
* Promote effective coordination among project delivery teams, project managers, technical leaders, and functional leadership.
* Provide visibility into project and portfolio needs to support informed operational decisions.
* Help balance project requirements, staff development opportunities, and business priorities.

Client and Business Support
  
  

* Support project teams in establishing clear client expectations and maintaining effective communication throughout project execution.
* Participate in client discussions when senior project-delivery leadership or issue resolution is needed.
* Collaborate with business-development and proposal teams to develop achievable execution strategies, staffing plans, schedules, and budgets for new opportunities.
* Apply lessons learned from active and completed projects to improve future proposals and delivery plans.
* Support the transition of awarded work from business development into project execution.
* Help strengthen client confidence through reliable, transparent, and consistent project delivery.

Leadership and Collaboration
  
  

* Build strong working relationships across TPPSA, 1898 & Co., and Burns & McDonnell.
* Promote a collaborative environment in which project, technical, and business leaders share accountability for successful project outcomes.
* Lead through influence and help teams navigate competing priorities, organizational change, and complex delivery issues.
* Reinforce Burns & McDonnell’s culture, values, and commitment to client service.
* Support broader company and 1898 & Co. initiatives related to project delivery, operational excellence, and profitable growth.

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, construction management, project management, or a related field from an accredited program.
* Significant experience leading the delivery of consulting, engineering, infrastructure, or other professional-services projects.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple projects, programs, or a portfolio of work.
* Experience leading and developing project managers, project delivery managers, or other project-delivery professionals.
* Strong understanding of project financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, earned revenue, profitability, and change management.
* Demonstrated ability to identify project risks, address performance issues, and guide teams through project recovery.
* Experience supporting proposals, project planning, contract execution, and client communication.
* Transmission planning, power systems, electric utility, or energy-industry experience is preferred.
* Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to communicate complex project and business information clearly to project teams, leadership, and clients.
* Ability to lead through influence and work effectively across organizational and technical boundaries.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
* Experience with project-management, financial-management, or portfolio-reporting systems is preferred.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, architecture, business or related degree from accredited program and 13 years related professional experience required.
* Previous leadership and/or management experience is preferable.
* Must demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills, strong interpersonal skills, and the ability to clearly and effectively present complex information to all levels of employees, management, and clients.
* Position requires the ability to thoughtfully and positively influence, lead, and manage change.
* Must possess strong people management skills, interpersonal skills, project management experience, and a strategic perspective.
* Must be proficient in the use of computer software (i.e., Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

We've cleared $750M in bookings and turned a profit three years running. Founded in Austin in 2013, we're a team of about 180 that scales past 500 employees during peak season. You'll start as an individual contributor with no direct reports, in a new seat reporting directly to the COO. Your first owned area will be building Service Delivery into a working operational function. This will entail adding structure, visibility and process to the way we ensure as many customer jobs as possible are completed successfully and on time by LawnStarter Pros, in lawn care and other services we offer now and over time.

New projects will show up unscoped over time. That's by design. As LawnStarter enters new verticals and grows toward a multi-billion-dollar future, big problems will keep surfacing with no obvious owner, and you'll be one of the people the COO trusts to run them down.

**What makes this role different:**

* You work on some of the biggest company-wide projects, cutting across teams and functional areas.
* You'll be a top builder in Brain, LawnStarter's internal AI toolkit built on Claude Code that already powers everything we do across the company: metric queries, document drafting, bug triage, and more. We expect you to approach your work in an AI-first fashion, leveraging Brain to build new systems and processes that will push the limits of how fast AI can accelerate business results. Every project you run is built AI-first: the analysis, the tooling, the process automation, the monitoring. You build it yourself instead of waiting on an analyst or engineer.

You'll help define the standards we should meet for job completion rates and speed, measure whether we hit them, and design processes, incentives and real-time interventions that get tested with Pros and customers in the field to lift performance. Scope covers every vertical and every delivery model, from today's 1099 Pros to potential W-2 crews under future evaluation.

You'll define the standard for what a Pro should deliver, then build the agents and pipelines that measure adherence to it and run the tests that change behaviors and outcomes in the field.

**Move metrics.** Leverage systems thinking and AI expertise to drive business results that sit across various functional teams. That means untangling handoffs where several teams touch a problem or goal and no one team owns the outcome.

**Take unscoped problems from ideas to fully-running and automated systems.** Some of the most important work here hasn't been named yet. Mitigating EO risks and supporting survivors are a key priority given the scale of EO contamination with 2335 civilian casualties recorded between December 2024 and June 2026.

UNMAS play a central role in reducing harm through non-technical survey, EO disposal and clearance, inclusive risk education integrated with critical services such as education, agriculture, and cash/livelihoods, and sensitive community engagement, while facilitating referrals to survey and clearance actors where feasible.

The Red Hat Hybrid Platforms Product Management team is looking for a Principal Product Manager (technical) to own and drive identity solutions in Red Hat OpenShift.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
In this role, you are responsible for how people, workloads, and software agents authenticate to OpenShift and how OpenShift decides what they are allowed to do. You will work with the Engineering and Product teams who build and deliver those capabilities. The product area includes:
  
  

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will contribute to company strategy and work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Support, Sales, Security, and Field teams.
  
  
You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.
  
  
As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).

* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions

* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory

In this role, you are responsible for how people, workloads, and software agents authenticate to OpenShift and how OpenShift decides what they are allowed to do. You will work with the Engineering and Product teams who build and deliver those capabilities. The product area includes:
  
  

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will contribute to company strategy and work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Support, Sales, Security, and Field teams.
  
  
You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.
  
  
As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

**What You Will Bring**

* 5+ years of enterprise software experience in product management, technical marketing, solutions engineering, or a similar technical product or customer-facing role
* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).
* Working knowledge of cloud workload identity. Depth in at least one of the following, and literacy in the others: AWS STS, Microsoft Entra workload identity, and Google Workload Identity or Workload Identity Federation
* A clear view of how a typical enterprise uses identity: single sign-on, group-based access, joiner-mover-leaver, non-human identities, and short-lived credentials as the default
* A clear view of how identity should work for agentic AI.
* Linux skills and direct experience with Linux containers and Kubernetes
* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions
* Ability to handle several competing priorities
* Bachelor's or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Willingness to travel up to 25%

**The Following Are Considered a Plus**

* Hands-on configuration of OpenShift identity providers, OAuth, external OpenID Connect, or cloud credential modes used by managed OpenShift
* Upstream participation in Kubernetes SIG Auth or a related CNCF project
* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory
* Understanding of zero trust principles.
* Experience with compliance programs in which identity is a control, such as FedRAMP or PCI
* Prior experience with agile delivery and with Jira or a similar tool
* A track record of enterprise product launches

+ Demonstrated ability to collaborate on project timelines and maintaining project and technical documentation.
+ Experience working collaboratively across diverse teams and stakeholders.

+ Current OpenShift expertise: cluster architecture, GitOps, multi-cluster management, security and observability, GPU-enabled nodes.
+ Experience with Red Hat AI or its upstreams: OpenShift AI, vLLM, model serving with KServe, model registries and pipelines, and at least one of llm-d, LLM Compressor or Eval Hub.
+ Working knowledge of how enterprises run generative AI today: inference economics, model selection and optimization, RAG and evaluation, agent frameworks and harnesses, MCP, and the governance and cost pressures that shape production decisions.
+ Application development fluency on Kubernetes: containers, APIs, CI/CD and the trusted software supply chain (SBOM, signing, policy gates), in at least one of Python, Go or Java.
+ Hands-on experience with Ansible Automation Platform for enterprise automation, including event-driven workflows, or the capability to rapidly transition skills from comparable tools.
+ Experience delivering hands-on technical implementations based on architectural designs in enterprise environments.
+ Ability to meet stakeholder needs and carry-out expectations regarding project timelines, technical deliverables, and scope of work.

The Red Hat Hybrid Platforms Product Management team is looking for a Principal Product Manager (technical) to own and drive identity solutions in Red Hat OpenShift.

In this role, you are responsible for how people, workloads, and software agents authenticate to OpenShift and how OpenShift decides what they are allowed to do. You will work with the Engineering and Product teams who build and deliver those capabilities. The product area includes:

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will contribute to company strategy and work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Support, Sales, Security, and Field teams.

You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.

As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.

**What you will do:**
---------------------

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

**What you will bring:**
------------------------

* 5+ years of enterprise software experience in product management, technical marketing, solutions engineering, or a similar technical product or customer-facing role
* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).
* Working knowledge of cloud workload identity. Depth in at least one of the following, and literacy in the others: AWS STS, Microsoft Entra workload identity, and Google Workload Identity or Workload Identity Federation
* A clear view of how a typical enterprise uses identity: single sign-on, group-based access, joiner-mover-leaver, non-human identities, and short-lived credentials as the default
* A clear view of how identity should work for agentic AI.
* Linux skills and direct experience with Linux containers and Kubernetes
* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions
* Ability to handle several competing priorities
* Bachelor's or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Willingness to travel up to 25%

**The following are considered a plus:**
----------------------------------------

* Hands-on configuration of OpenShift identity providers, OAuth, external OpenID Connect, or cloud credential modes used by managed OpenShift
* Upstream participation in Kubernetes SIG Auth or a related CNCF project
* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory
* Understanding of zero trust principles.
* Experience with compliance programs in which identity is a control, such as FedRAMP or PCI
* Prior experience with agile delivery and with Jira or a similar tool
* A track record of enterprise product launches

The Analytics Manager will be responsible for leveraging operational analytics to explore the relationship between customer experience data and financial metrics, such as churn, cost to serve and profitability, as well as overseeing and managing the financial planning and analysis activities within the CX department. This role also encompasses strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, monitoring of expenditures related to both operational activities and capital initiatives, aimed at improving customer experience and meeting its financial objectives.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Customer Experience and Financial Metrics**

* Explore and analyze the relationship between customer experience (CX) data and financial metrics, such as chrurn, cost to serve and profitability.
* Provide insights to support decision-making that balances customer satisfaction with financial performance.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align CX initiatives with cost management strategies.

**Operational Analytics and Efficiency**

* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate operational effectiveness and cost efficiency, trade-offs with customer experience
* Conduct operational analytics to identify opportunities for process improvements and cost optimization.
* Lead initiatives aimed at enhancing productivity and achieving measurable savings.

* Lead the development and management of budgeting and forecasting processes to support business objectives and operational requirements.

* Collaborate with business units and finance teams to ensure accurate financial reporting and monthly accruals.
